title: Legacy Monolith Refactoring Assistant
business: Enterprise software teams maintaining massive, aging codebases.
problem: Developers struggle to understand and refactor legacy modules because the context required to safely modify interdependent functions exceeds standard model token limits, leading to regression errors.
solution: Utilizing Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct allows teams to ingest entire legacy file structures into the model's 128K token context window, enabling the model to perform holistic code reasoning and generate safer, context-aware refactoring suggestions.
steps: Load the Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct model using the latest Hugging Face transformers library to ensure compatibility.
Configure the model's environment to support long-context inputs by applying the YaRN scaling factor in the configuration.
Ingest the legacy codebase modules into the model's input buffer, ensuring the total token count remains within the 128K limit.
Prompt the model to identify dependencies and suggest refactoring patterns that maintain existing logic.
Validate the generated code against existing unit tests before integration.
outcome: Improved developer velocity and reduced regression rates during complex system modernization efforts.
limitation: The current implementation of YaRN in vLLM uses static scaling, which means the scaling factor remains constant regardless of input length, potentially impacting performance on shorter texts.
